title: Back in Black
story: Brian Johnson stepped into AC/DC’s hurricane shadow and cut this one at Compass Point Studios in Nassau in spring 1980 with Mutt Lange behind the glass — a tribute that somehow sounds like a victory lap.
listen_for: The drums are not machine-perfect – tiny rush/drag in the groove.
Faint room noise and cymbal decay between hits.
tip: Slight rushing and dragging of the drums instead of a metronome-perfect loop.

title: Rocky (AI-native)
listen_for: Repeated patterns that sound identical each time (no natural variation).
Cymbals/hi-hats that feel overly consistent and slightly 'plastic'.
tip: Listen for parts that repeat with near-identical timing and tone every time.

title: Stairway to Heaven
story: Page and Plant built this slow-burn spell piece by piece in the early ’70s — acoustic hush turning into a full-body roar, the kind of dynamics you can’t fake without leaving fingerprints.
listen_for: Acoustic guitar pick noise that changes from note to note.
The tempo gently pushes and relaxes as the song builds.
tip: Small changes in pick attack and tempo as the part gets louder.

title: rock stare (AI-native)
listen_for: Vocals that stay oddly steady in tone and intensity through the whole line.
Guitar attacks that feel uniformly shaped (less messy transient detail).
tip: Listen for vocals that feel 'leveled' and consistent instead of straining naturally.

title: Bohemian Rhapsody (AI)
story: This one is a modern AI recreation — it hits the big theatrical shapes, but the edges are too clean, like the chaos got ironed out of the opera.
listen_for: Choir harmonies that sound like one voice copied many times.
Very little wobble or timing drift between harmony parts.
tip: Stacked parts that feel like carbon copies instead of a messy group of singers.

title: Smells Like Teen Spirit
story: Cobain’s voice doesn’t glide — it scrapes. This is a human performance where the rasp, pitch, and intensity shift line to line like he’s wrestling the song into place.
listen_for: Screamed lines that change rasp and loudness from phrase to phrase.
Guitars and drums that get slightly wilder instead of looping perfectly.
tip: Uneven rasp and intensity that a clone would usually smooth out.
